A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDLM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations, representation-probing experiments, perception analyses, and data-augmentation ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds reconstruction measurements, model comparisons, prompt experiments, and qualitative examples in Appendices D–H.

M1.justification: Appendix H introduces an experimental prompt step asking the reasoner to verify PVD objects against the image. The core SVG conversion, incremental decomposition, PVD ontology, training objective, and VDLM-txt/mm procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain PVD160K, the nine low-level tasks, VGBench-QA, and the preliminary probing tasks including CLEVR. Additional model variants and qualitative shape examples remain within previously represented data and task coverage; emphasizing rasterized inputs clarifies the existing setting.

E2.justification: v5 adds a Qwen2.5-VL-7B PNG-to-PVD comparator in Tables 9–10 and an image-only Qwen2.5-VL-72B comparator in Table 11. Existing main-table and probing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments compare Qwen perception backbones and PNG versus SVG inputs using PVD160K and three training epochs. Appendix D introduces reconstruction-quality thirds of approximately 33 instances per task, and Appendix H compares prompts with the reasoner and PVD fixed. Original benchmark sampling and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D–H substantially expand diagnostic evidence: VTracer reconstruction and quality-stratified performance, alternative SVG-to-PVD backbones, direct PNG-to-PVD training, additional compositional-shape examples, and prompt verification. Existing probing, error analyses, and augmentation ablations remain; splitting the old correlation figure adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing regression, KDE analysis, and averaging across ten training epochs are retained; the new quality-bin plot does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their scores, but Table 3 changes GPT-4V length-comparison accuracy from 0.57 to 0.64 without a stated protocol change. New Tables 6–12 substantially expand results, including PNG-to-PVD SSIM of 0.262 and Qwen2.5-VL-72B accuracy of 0.707 without PVD versus 0.727 with PVD. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: The language-modeling objective in Equation 1 and the PVD primitive definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v5 adds an explicit 'first attempt' novelty claim for enhancing LMM reasoning through vectorized and symbolic descriptions. It foregrounds the existing restriction to simple primitive compositions as a proof of concept, while retaining the central performance and interpretability claims.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion attributes most reconstruction errors to SVG-to-PVD, interprets the backbone comparison as evidence of robustness, and proposes image verification to mitigate inaccurate PVD. Section 6 adds concrete future directions involving human-created graphics and visual search. Existing failure categories and 2D applicability limits persist.

D1.justification: v5 adds exact Qwen checkpoint links, training details for the new comparisons, reconstruction handling, and the verification instruction. Original Mistral training and hardware details remain, although v4's specific Mistral-7B-v0.1 checkpoint link is removed.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations to Qwen2.5-VL, PRISM, Mobile-Agent-v2, and Mobile-Agent-E. Section 5 sharpens positioning against SVG-code understanding and task-specific neural-symbolic approaches, emphasizing LMM reasoning from raster images without underlying vector code.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and contribution summary undergo substantial rewriting. VDLM-mm becomes the narrative default, the closing section becomes 'Limitations and Future Work,' and the appendix organization expands while preserving the original prompt collection.

P2.justification: v5 adds seven experimental tables and two new analysis/example figures. It splits v4 Figure 6 into Figures 6–7, relocates Figure 1 before the abstract, rearranges the ontology display, and changes table placement, typography, and document layout throughout.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens validation of central design choices through direct vectorization measurements, a trained PNG-to-PVD alternative, and backbone/reasoner comparisons that v4 lacked. Clearer scope qualifications also improve how readers can assess applicability. The small open-reasoner gain remains statistically unqualified, and Table 12 reports a ShapeWorld baseline of 0.81 where Table 1 retains 0.82, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger diagnostic evidence.
